meta.title: Homelab architecture
meta.subtitle: Four hosts, 39 containers, one storage pool — and how they actually depend on each other.
meta.note: Structure is curated and versioned here; live health is overlaid at runtime from the newest homelab-doctor report.

zones.label: Edge
zones.description: The gateway between the LAN and the WAN.

categories.label: Network & DNS
categories.description: Name resolution, DHCP, reverse proxies, VPN tunnel, gateway.

categories.label: Storage
categories.description: Physical disks, the ZFS pool, the Samba export and every CIFS mount that consumes it.

categories.label: Media
categories.description: Jellyfin, Kavita, the *arr automation stack and the download clients.

categories.label: Platform

hosts.label: Off-LAN
hosts.notes: Nothing here is reachable inbound. Every link crossing this boundary is outbound-initiated from inside the LAN.

hosts.label: Router / Gateway
hosts.notes: Upstream DNS target for Pi-hole. Since Sept 2026 it is also the LAN's DHCP server — Pi-hole's own DHCP must stay OFF, or the two servers race and present as 'all the servers are down'.

hosts.label: rpi
hosts.notes: Lowest-powered host, and deliberately kept to just DNS (Pi-hole) plus a Dozzle log-shipping agent since the app tier moved to opti 2026-09-10 and DHCP moved to the router in Sept 2026. It is still the LAN's sole DNS server, so losing it still takes name resolution down. Boots from a 220 GB USB SSD since the microSD card it used to run on died 2026-09-08.

hosts.label: opti

facts.label: Containers
facts.value: 18 (13 app tier + Pertal, Seerr, 3 Cockpit gateways) + CI/control services

hosts.notes: Every other host mounts its Samba export, so it is the storage single point of failure. Since the 2026-07-25 ZFS migration the live share [red] is configured in /etc/homelab/samba-red.conf — OMV is UI/monitoring only and no longer owns the share. Also hosts the agent control plane and the x86 CI runner. Since 2026-09-10 it also runs the whole app tier (dashboard, Vaultwarden, notes, Dozzle hub, 5 Discord bots) — so an opti outage now costs those services too, not just storage and control. Also runs Pertal (dashboard v4, :8444), Seerr (media requests) and the three Cockpit console gateways. Boot disk (sdb) has 272 reallocated sectors, creeping ~8 every two months; pending/uncorrectable both still 0. The weekly attic cold copy was retired 2026-09-24, so pool red currently has no second copy.

hosts.label: noblenumbat
hosts.notes: A laptop with sleep masked. Hardware-transcodes for Jellyfin via /dev/dri/renderD128. Suffered a whole-host outage from a cooling problem on 2026-07-16 — thermals are the thing to watch here. Also hosts Uptime Kuma (:3001, moved off opti 2026-09-10 so it watches opti from outside) and ntfy (:2586, the homelab's push server, added 2026-09-24) — both deliberately off opti for the same reason.

hosts.label: tux
hosts.role: Workstation — where the code is written
hosts.notes: One workstation, dual-booted: tux (CachyOS) and ptm (Windows 11). The git working copy is a local disk on the Windows side, so edits reach the homelab only through git push and CI — opti's repo copy is a CI deploy snapshot, not a checkout. Not a server: only the optional Windows-side asset server (:8767) is consumed by anything.

hosts.label: android (S10)
hosts.notes: Intermittent by nature — a phone. Its DNS record is static but it drops off the LAN often; the webapp's LLM tab degrades gracefully. Was unreachable during the probe that produced this map.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.notes: Both self-hosted runners poll GitHub outbound over HTTPS, so no inbound port is ever opened. This is the only path by which outside code reaches the LAN.

nodes.label: VPN exit — Netherlands
nodes.notes: All torrent/usenet/indexer traffic egresses here, never via the LAN's own WAN IP.

nodes.label: Phone · away from home
nodes.notes: The Archer's exported config points DNS at 10.213.87.1 (its own forwarder — no LAN names). It is hand-edited to DNS = 192.168.1.10, and a re-export from the router silently reverts that edit.

nodes.label: Gateway 192.168.1.1
nodes.notes: DHCP must remain disabled here. When it is re-enabled it races Pi-hole and hands out leases pointing at the wrong DNS — the classic 'servers are down' symptom. Also the LAN's WireGuard server: UDP :51820 on the WAN side, tunnel subnet 10.213.87.0/24, routed into the LAN without NAT — no homelab host runs wg.

nodes.label: Pi-hole
nodes.notes: v6 (FTL v6.7). DNS only for the whole 192.168.1.0/24 — DHCP moved to the router (TP-Link Archer) in Sept 2026. 15 local A records, 6 static MAC reservations. Whitelist with `pihole allow`.

nodes.label: nginx (webapp)
nodes.notes: Terminates TLS for webapp.lan using a cert read directly off opti's local pool (bind mount, no CIFS now that it runs on opti). Raises proxy_read_timeout to 240s for /api/llama/ only — cold LLM prompts legitimately exceed nginx's 60s default.

nodes.label: docker net · internal
nodes.notes: Every opti app-tier service shares this bridge. Bot control APIs bind :8080 on it and are NOT published to the host, so only the webapp can reach them.

nodes.label: Dashboard webapp
nodes.notes: webapp.v3.Fable: a Vite-built frontend behind a Node/Express backend, deployed by CI on opti — there is no live-on-copy path, a change reaches webapp.lan only once it is committed, pushed and opti-apps-deploy.yml runs. Reads agent-logs and security-reports directly off the local pool (bind mount, no CIFS since it moved here 2026-09-10) and proxies the bot control APIs, the opti dispatcher and the phone's LLM.

nodes.label: Pertal (dashboard v4)
nodes.notes: The v4 dashboard, live side by side with v3 until cutover (when it takes :8443). Behind nginx-webapp's :8444 listener. Built and started last by opti-apps-deploy.yml under the 'pertal' compose profile, so a failed Pertal build never blocks a v3 deploy. Shares the arch_data volume with v3 and fronts the Cockpit console gateways, Seerr requests and the Readarr books panel.

nodes.label: Seerr
nodes.notes: Jellyseerr's successor. Signs in with Jellyfin and hands approved requests to Sonarr/Radarr on noblenumbat. Pertal's Requests page reads and approves via SEERR_API_KEY. Image pinned deliberately — bump by hand.

nodes.label: Notes app
nodes.notes: Published directly on the host as well as proxied, so phones can skip the self-signed-cert prompt.

nodes.label: MariaDB
nodes.notes: Holds the password vault. The single most backup-critical dataset here.

nodes.label: discord-weather
nodes.notes: Manage via the webapp's #weather tab — never by editing files on opti.

nodes.label: discord-hltv
nodes.notes: The container is `discord-hltv`, not `discord-cs2` — the compose service and the container name differ from what the CS2 naming elsewhere suggests.

nodes.label: hltv-api
nodes.notes: Backs discord-hltv (and other consumers) with cached HLTV match data.

nodes.label: Actions runner (ARM64)
nodes.notes: Pinned to [self-hosted, ARM64] because a bare 'self-hosted' label also matched opti's x86 runner. Only deploys rpi's own small stack now that the app tier lives on opti.

nodes.label: /mnt/opti-fs
nodes.notes: How the rpi used to read agent logs, security reports, TLS certs and the repo back when the webapp ran here. Since the app tier moved to opti (2026-09-10) nothing uses this mount — docker-stack-logs.service, its last consumer, was disabled 2026-09-27. Left mounted but idle.

nodes.label: Uptime Kuma
nodes.notes: Part of the 2026-08-02 control-hub work: probes every service on its own schedule, independent of the collector cadence. On noblenumbat (host network) since 2026-09-10, so it watches opti from outside.

nodes.label: Dozzle
nodes.notes: The Dozzle hub itself, since 2026-09-10 (moved off rpi along with the rest of the app tier). Streams opti's own containers directly over the local docker socket, plus rpi's and noblenumbat's via their dozzle-agents on :7007.

nodes.label: sdc · 4 TB WD Red Plus
nodes.notes: The single vdev backing pool red. One disk = no redundancy, and since the attic cold copy was retired 2026-09-24 there is no second copy of this data.

nodes.label: ZFS pool · red
nodes.notes: Replaced the mergerfs pool on 2026-07-25. Datasets: red/fs (the Samba share root) and red/media. This is the homelab's primary dataset — media, repo, certs, agent logs, security reports all live here. Single-vdev: a scrub verifies integrity but nothing self-heals without a mirror. The weekly attic cold copy was retired 2026-09-24, so this pool currently has NO second copy.

nodes.label: Samba · share [red]
nodes.notes: Exports red/fs as \\opti\red. Config lives in /etc/homelab/samba-red.conf — hand-managed since the ZFS migration; OMV no longer owns the live share.

nodes.label: sdb · 500 GB HDD
nodes.notes: opti's boot disk — device letters on opti are NOT stable, this was sda before 2026-09-10. 272 reallocated sectors, creeping ~8 every two months; pending/uncorrectable both still 0. Holds only the OS — app data and homelab.db live on pool red, so its death costs a reinstall, not data.

nodes.label: sda · 596 GB HDD
nodes.sublabel: Hitachi HTS5475 · NTFS · unused, mounted ro
nodes.notes: Formerly an attic cold-copy branch; unused since the attic/coldcopy retirement 2026-09-24. Mounted read-only at /srv/dev-disk-by-uuid-C682C2DE82C2D1DB.

nodes.label: OpenMediaVault
nodes.notes: Demoted at the ZFS migration: disk/SMART monitoring and UI only. The live share is NOT in OMV's smb.conf anymore.

nodes.label: Agent dispatcher
nodes.notes: The LAN control plane the webapp's Agents tab drives. Runs from the repo checkout on the OMV data disk.

nodes.label: Homelab agents
nodes.notes: SSH out to every host, then write JSON reports into the pool. The homelab-doctor report is what this page's live overlay reads.

nodes.label: agent-logs/
nodes.notes: hardware-latest · software-latest · network-latest · homelab-doctor-latest. The rpi webapp mounts this read-only at /agent-logs.

nodes.label: homelab.db
nodes.notes: Everything the homelab knows, as rows: collector history back to June 2026, host inventory, container change history, and FTS over every runbook. Deliberately on its own dataset OUTSIDE the Samba-exported red/fs — SQLite WAL over CIFS is unsafe, so only opti-local processes open it.

nodes.label: homelab-db server
nodes.notes: Serves the webapp's Data page and the `homelab` MCP tools a Claude Code session uses. Bearer token + Origin/Host validation; MCP pinned to spec 2025-06-18.

nodes.label: Cockpit gateway · opti
nodes.notes: SSH-to-bridge gateway for the Pertal Console: full root Cockpit on opti with no login, reachable only from Pertal over the private cockpit_gw bridge (172.30.90.0/24) — port 9090 is never published, and nginx returns 404 for /cp-*. Bypasses Pertal jobs/audit and holds. See apps/cockpit-gw/README.md.

nodes.label: Cockpit gateway · rpi
nodes.notes: Same gateway as cockpit-opti, targeting ptm@192.168.1.10. Runs on opti, not on the rpi — the rpi stays a 2-container DNS appliance.

nodes.label: Cockpit gateway · noblenumbat
nodes.notes: Same gateway as cockpit-opti, targeting ptm@192.168.1.6.

nodes.label: systemd timers
nodes.sublabel: docs 05:16 · health-digest 06:30 · autoreboot · zfs scrub 2nd Sun (cron)

nodes.label: Gluetun VPN
nodes.notes: Five containers share this network namespace, so if gluetun stops they lose all connectivity — that is the intended kill-switch. Its NAT-PMP port forwarding dies silently; the vpn-stack-heal timer exists to catch that.

nodes.label: vpn-stack-heal
nodes.notes: Watchdog added 2026-07-11 after Gluetun's forwarded port kept dying without any error. Re-syncs the forwarded port into qBittorrent. Status at /var/lib/vpn-stack-heal/status.json.

nodes.label: stream-station
nodes.notes: Server-side vlcwatcher, added 2026-08-07: streamlink resolves a Twitch/YouTube/Kick channel (skipping the site player and its ads) and headless VLC remuxes it to HLS for the dashboard's Streams page. Four independent slots. REMUX ONLY, never transcode — the sources are already H.264+AAC, so a live 1080p stream costs ~3.5% CPU; that is deliberate, this host has a cooling outage on record (2026-07-16). Segments live on a 256M tmpfs at /hls and never touch the NVMe. The ONLY built-not-pulled service in the YAMS stack (python:3.12-slim + VLC + pip streamlink, runs as uid 1000 because VLC refuses to run as root), so the deploy workflow copies its build context and runs `docker compose build`. Plain yams_network, NOT gluetun — VPN is opt-in there. POST /start|/stop are bearer-token gated (HL_STREAM_TOKEN, matched against the rpi webapp's env); GET /hls/* is open so browsers can fetch segments through nginx. An idle reaper stops any slot whose playlist has not been fetched for 5 minutes, so nothing pulls a stream unattended. It is the only container in this stack with mem_limit/cpus caps.

nodes.label: Audiobookshelf
nodes.notes: Added 2026-10-03. Library is a hardlinked Author/Series/Vol tree under audiobooks/library on noblenumbat's local NVMe (not opti's pool), so torrents keep seeding from their own folders. Defined only in the on-host /opt/yams/docker-compose.custom.yaml, not yet in the repo's compose.

nodes.label: Readarr (BookshelfNG)
nodes.notes: BookshelfNG fork with native Hardcover metadata, added 2026-10-03. Imports into /data/books — Kavita's Books library, on the local NVMe. Its own auto-search is unreliable; working route is pushing real magnets via /api/v1/release/push. Host port 8788 because 8787 is a host python3 service. Defined only in the on-host /opt/yams/docker-compose.custom.yaml, not yet in the repo's compose.

nodes.label: Prowlarr
nodes.notes: Feeds indexers to every *arr. Published through gluetun's port map, not its own.

nodes.label: qBittorrent
nodes.notes: Version-pinned deliberately. Its listen port must track Gluetun's forwarded port or nothing seeds — that sync is what vpn-stack-heal maintains.

nodes.label: Docker engine
nodes.notes: Stack lives at /opt/yams/docker-compose.yaml. Watchtower was removed 2026-07-25; image updates are now report-only (software-inventory) and applied deliberately via docker compose pull. Since 2026-08-07 the deploy workflow also copies build contexts and runs `docker compose build` — stream-station is built here, not pulled, so the pull step passes --ignore-buildable.

nodes.label: opti CIFS mounts
nodes.notes: Movies, Shows and the import inbox all live on opti, not locally. Jellyfin's libraries are these mounts — if opti or the LAN blips, playback stops.

nodes.label: media-import
nodes.notes: Sweeps the Media-Import inbox on opti's pool into the library.

nodes.label: ntfy
nodes.notes: The homelab's phone push server, added 2026-09-24/25 — off opti for the same reason as Uptime Kuma, so it still works if opti is down. homelab/tools/notify.py posts alerts here on topic 'homelab'.

nodes.label: tux workstation
nodes.sublabel: Editor + Claude Code · repo at E:\REPO\ptm4

nodes.label: llama-server
nodes.notes: Offline local inference, ~40s warm. The webapp's LLM tab and the `ask` runbook helper both target it. Was offline during this probe.

edges.label: SSH as ptm → root Cockpit bridge
SSH as ptm → root Cockpit bridge
SSH as ptm → root Cockpit bridge
reads agent-logs directly off the pool
TLS cert read directly off the pool (local bind mount)
builds the Vite frontend and restarts the container

edges.notes: Same-origin on purpose: the dashboard is https, so a <video> pointed straight at http://192.168.1.6:8098 would be blocked as mixed content. These are unauthenticated GETs — playlists and segments only.

edges.label: /api/streams → :8098 (control)
edges.notes: Start/stop/status/presets/keepalive. The bearer token is injected here, server-side, so it never reaches the browser and only the dashboard can start a stream.

edges.label: streamlink resolves twitch/youtube/kick
edges.notes: Direct LAN egress, not through gluetun — VPN membership on this host is opt-in per service. A geo-locked source would use gluetun's HTTP proxy on :8888 rather than joining its netns.

flows.name: A movie, from request to playback
flows.summary: The full media path — and the reason the VPN and the NAS both sit in the middle of it.

steps.title: Prowlarr feeds indexers to Radarr
steps.detail: Prowlarr holds the indexer definitions centrally; each *arr asks it rather than keeping its own copies.

steps.title: Radarr hands the release to qBittorrent
steps.detail: Radarr picks a release and pushes it to the download client over the shared docker network.

steps.title: qBittorrent has no network of its own
steps.detail: It runs with network_mode: service:gluetun, so its only route out is the tunnel. Stop gluetun and it goes dark — that is the kill-switch working.

steps.title: Gluetun egresses in the Netherlands
steps.detail: Public IP 46.29.25.130, with NAT-PMP forwarded port 42328 mapped back to qBittorrent's listen port.

steps.title: The finished file is written to opti, not locally
steps.detail: Downloads land on the CIFS mount, so the 468 GB NVMe never fills with media.

steps.title: Radarr imports it into the library
steps.detail: Rename and move within opti's pool — a metadata operation on the same filesystem.

steps.title: Jellyfin sees it via /mnt/opti-library
steps.detail: Its libraries ARE the opti mounts; there is no local copy of the media.

steps.title: You stream it on :8096
steps.detail: Transcoding, when needed, is hardware-accelerated on the UHD 620 via /dev/dri/renderD128.

flows.name: Watching a live stream in the browser
flows.summary: The Streams page: why the video and the controls reach the same container by two different routes.

steps.title: You open /streams/ on the dashboard
steps.detail: A standalone page with four slot tabs. Only the active tab holds a player; the other slots keep running on the server.

steps.title: Pressing a preset POSTs /api/streams/start
steps.detail: The Express backend forwards it to stream-station on noblenumbat and injects the bearer token server-side, so the browser never sees a credential and only this dashboard can start a stream.

steps.title: streamlink resolves the channel
steps.detail: It pulls the raw stream from Twitch/YouTube/Kick instead of the site's web player, which is what skips the ads. Egress is direct over the LAN — this container is deliberately not in gluetun's netns.

steps.title: VLC remuxes it to HLS on a tmpfs
steps.detail: cvlc cuts the H.264+AAC source into 2-second segments under /hls on a 256M tmpfs. Nothing is transcoded and nothing is written to the NVMe — ~3.5% CPU for a live 1080p stream, which is what keeps this thermally safe on a laptop.

steps.title: The browser fetches segments back through nginx
steps.detail: Served same-origin at /hls so the https page can play them; hls.js rides ~2 segments behind the edge, putting you roughly 8-12 seconds behind live. Stop watching and the idle reaper stops the slot after 5 minutes.

flows.name: Shipping a change to this dashboard
flows.summary: How code on the workstation becomes a running container on opti — with no inbound port ever opened.

steps.title: Edit on the workstation, then git push to main
steps.detail: The working copy is E:\REPO\ptm4 on the workstation's own disk — nothing on opti is edited by hand. Pushing paths under homelab/hosts/opti/apps/webapp.v3.Fable/** is what triggers the deploy workflow for the live dashboard.

steps.title: opti's own runner picks up the job
steps.detail: The runner polls GitHub outbound over HTTPS, on opti itself. Nothing is exposed inbound — this is the only way external code enters the LAN.

steps.title: The Vite frontend is built and shipped
steps.detail: webapp.v3.Fable is built by CI and deployed straight into opti's compose stack — there is no live-on-copy path. A change reaches webapp.lan only once this workflow (opti-apps-deploy.yml) runs.

steps.title: compose pull + up -d reconciles the stack
steps.detail: Images are refreshed for the app tier and the stack reconciled, then the webapp container restarts to re-exec the Node process. Pertal and the Cockpit gateways sit behind compose profiles and are started explicitly, last.

flows.name: Resolving a name on the LAN
flows.summary: Why the rpi stays load-bearing for DNS even though DHCP moved off it.
flows.risk: DNS lives in one container on rpi, which now boots from a USB SSD (the microSD it used to run on died 2026-09-08). If Pi-hole's DHCP is ever turned back on it will race the router's and hand out leases with the wrong DNS — which presents as 'all the servers are down'.

steps.title: A device gets its DHCP lease from the router
steps.detail: The TP-Link Archer has served DHCP for 192.168.1.0/24 since Sept 2026 — Pi-hole's own DHCP was turned off to stop the two servers racing. Scope .2–.250, with six MAC-pinned reservations for the servers.

steps.title: Every lookup goes to 192.168.1.10:53
steps.detail: Ad-blocking plus the 15 local A records (webapp.lan, jellyfin.lan, comics.lan, opti.lan…) that make the homelab addressable by name.

steps.title: Unknown names go upstream to the router
steps.detail: 192.168.1.1 is the primary upstream.

steps.title: Cloudflare is the fallback
steps.detail: 1.1.1.1 covers the case where the router's resolver is unhappy.

flows.name: How this page knows what is up
flows.summary: The agent loop that produces the live overlay on the Map tab.

steps.title: A timer on opti starts an agent run
steps.detail: homelab-doctor, plus the hardware, software and network reporters.

steps.title: Each agent SSHes out to every host
steps.detail: It collects containers, disks, packages and pool state first-hand.

steps.title: Results are written as JSON onto the pool
steps.detail: homelab-doctor-latest.json and friends land in /srv/red/fs/ptm/agent-logs/.

steps.title: The webapp reads them read-only
steps.detail: Since the webapp moved to opti (2026-09-10) this is a local bind mount of the pool at /agent-logs inside the container — no CIFS involved.

steps.title: Sync fetches /api/architecture/live
steps.detail: The route reshapes the newest doctor/hardware/software reports per host — no fresh SSH round trip, so the button is cheap.

flows.name: The VPN port-forward watchdog
flows.summary: A silent failure that needed a watchdog rather than a fix.

steps.title: Every 2 minutes, check the forwarded port
steps.detail: Gluetun's NAT-PMP lease dies without logging an error, so nothing surfaces the failure on its own.

steps.title: Push the port back into qBittorrent
steps.detail: If qBittorrent's listen port has drifted from the forwarded port, seeding silently stops. The healer re-syncs them.

steps.title: Confirm the tunnel still egresses in NL
steps.detail: Public IP and port are recorded to /var/lib/vpn-stack-heal/status.json — check there first when torrents stall.

flows.name: Reaching the homelab from the phone
flows.summary: The WireGuard path in from anywhere — terminating on the router, not on any homelab host.
flows.risk: Tunnel clients keep their 10.213.87.x source address, so any new LAN-only firewall rule will work on wifi and time out on VPN. And a profile re-exported from the Archer reverts DNS to 10.213.87.1, silently losing every LAN name.

steps.title: The phone brings up its tunnel
steps.detail: AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, so while connected everything the phone does routes through home.

steps.title: The Archer answers on UDP :51820
steps.detail: The router itself is the WireGuard server — no homelab host runs wg. Tunnel traffic (10.213.87.0/24) is routed into the LAN without NAT, so hosts see the raw tunnel IP.

steps.title: DNS rides the tunnel to Pi-hole
steps.detail: Two prerequisites: the client config's DNS line hand-edited to 192.168.1.10, and Pi-hole's listening mode set to ALL — the LOCAL default refused non-LAN sources. This is what makes webapp.rpi resolve remotely.

steps.title: The dashboard works exactly as on wifi
steps.detail: Same origin, same homelab-CA cert — the phone's trust store doesn't care which network the request rode in on.

steps.title: opti's share is reachable too
steps.detail: ufw on opti and noblenumbat needed explicit allow rules for 10.213.87.0/24 — without them VPN packets were silently dropped: the classic 5-second timeout.

flows.name: Opening the password vault
flows.summary: The shortest path in the homelab, and the one with the most valuable data behind it.

steps.title: HTTPS to bitwarden.rpi.lan
steps.detail: nginx terminates TLS on :443 with a local cert.

steps.title: Proxied to Vaultwarden
steps.detail: Vaultwarden itself is never published to the host — only nginx can reach it, over the internal docker bridge.

steps.title: Secrets are read from MariaDB
steps.detail: This dataset is the most backup-critical thing in the homelab. It has lived on opti since 2026-09-10, on pool red.

storage.summary: One ZFS pool on opti backs essentially everything. Every other host is a CIFS client of it. Migrated from mergerfs 2026-07-25; the old disks (the 'attic' cold copy) were retired 2026-09-24 and no longer hold a second copy.

branches.note: single vdev — no redundancy, and no second copy since the attic cold copy was retired 2026-09-24

layout.purpose: Agent JSON reports → webapp /agent-logs (local bind mount on opti)
Security agent output → webapp /reports (local bind mount on opti)
CI deploy snapshot of the repo (rsync, no .git) — opti's services run from it; never edited by hand
Deploy logs written by the CI runners

consumers.what: unused since 2026-09-27 — kept mounted, nothing reads it
the whole share, for files (the repo is edited locally, not here)

notes: The live share [red] is configured in /etc/homelab/samba-red.conf, hand-managed. OMV no longer owns it — its smb.conf is not where the share lives.

The pool is a single vdev: ZFS checksums detect corruption but cannot self-heal it without a mirror. The weekly attic cold copy (rsync --delete to the old mergerfs pair) was retired 2026-09-24, so pool red currently has no second copy at all — a mirror disk is the structural fix (see the opti-drive-onboard skill).

Since 2026-09-10 the app tier (dashboard, Vaultwarden, notes, Dozzle, 5 Discord bots) runs on opti itself and reads/writes the pool via local bind mounts, not CIFS — only the other hosts (rpi, noblenumbat, tux) are CIFS clients now.

agents.what: Cross-host service + container health. Feeds this page's live overlay.
CPU, RAM, disks, temperatures per host.
Audits units, timers and cron for unexpected persistence.

observations.title: DNS is a single point of failure, now on a USB SSD
observations.detail: Pi-hole on the rpi is the LAN's only DNS server — DHCP moved to the router in Sept 2026, so it's no longer a second job stacked on the same box. The rpi boots from a 220 GB USB SSD since the microSD card it used to run on died 2026-09-08. Losing that drive still takes name resolution down with it, though the USB SSD is far more durable than the SD card was.

observations.title: opti is the storage AND app-tier single point of failure
observations.detail: The rpi, noblenumbat and tux all mount //opti/red. Jellyfin's libraries, the TLS certs and the repo all live there. Since 2026-09-10 opti also runs the whole app tier (dashboard, vault, notes, bots), so an opti outage now costs storage, control plane and all of those services at once — while DNS (on rpi) keeps the LAN resolving names.

observations.title: One inbound path, and it is on the router
observations.detail: The only thing reachable from outside is the router's WireGuard server (UDP :51820); no homelab host listens on the WAN and nothing else is port-forwarded. Both CI runners reach GitHub outbound-only, so deploys work without exposing anything.

observations.title: The VPN kill-switch is real
observations.detail: Five containers share Gluetun's network namespace rather than merely routing through it, so they cannot leak to the WAN if the tunnel drops.

observations.title: The live pool has no redundancy — and no second copy at all
observations.detail: Pool red is a single 4 TB vdev. ZFS checksums catch corruption, but with no mirror nothing self-heals. The weekly attic cold copy was retired 2026-09-24, so there is currently no second copy of the pool whatsoever — a disk failure now costs everything since the last good state, not just a week. A mirror disk is the structural fix (see the opti-drive-onboard skill).

observations.title: Leftovers worth cleaning up
observations.detail: A vpn.rpi.lan DNS record and WireGuard peer configs survive a decommissioned service, and a stale pre-ZFS copy of the repo sits on opti's old NTFS disk (dev-disk-by-uuid…/fs/ptm/repo/ptm4) — one commit behind and no longer referenced by any unit.

observations.title: noblenumbat's real risk is thermal, not software
observations.detail: A whole-host outage on 2026-07-16 turned out to be a cooling problem on the laptop chassis, not a Jellyfin or container fault.
